narrative.overview: PDF and Image + is a calm, trustworthy utility, not a flashy product — the design has to earn the trust of someone about to drop a contract or ID scan into a browser tab. Every surface is flat: white or near-white panels sit on a faint indigo-tinted canvas, separated by hairline borders and tonal rings rather than drop shadows. The one deliberate piece of theater is a two-lane color system — indigo for every PDF tool, emerald for every image tool — carried from the homepage grid down to the logomark itself (two small rectangles, indigo and emerald, side by side). Nothing else competes for saturation: a deep indigo-900 hero and a couple of emerald checkmarks are the only concentrated color in an otherwise white, quiet interface. The voice is efficient and unpretentious: bold, tight headlines state the job to be done ("Merge PDF"), body copy stays short and literal, and trust signals (no sign-up, no watermark, no upload) are repeated as plain badges rather than marketing copy. Nothing here should read as decorative — every color, radius, and piece of motion answers "which lane am I in" or "did that click work."
keyCharacteristics: Two-lane color coding: indigo = PDF, emerald = Image, applied consistently to icons, tile borders, hover glow, and badges.
Flat surfaces by default; elevation only appears as a tinted glow on hover, never as ambient shadow at rest.
One saturated dark section (indigo-900 hero / CTA band) bookending otherwise white, quiet pages.
Generous, consistent corner rounding (17px tiles, 12px buttons, full pills) — no sharp corners anywhere.
Plus Jakarta Sans throughout; no secondary display face.

rules.name: The One Lane Rule
rules.body: A component is either in the indigo lane or the emerald lane, never both. If it represents a PDF tool or PDF-category content, every accent on it — icon, border, hover glow, badge — is indigo. Image-category content gets the emerald equivalent, token-for-token. Don't mix lanes within one component to imply "extra emphasis."

rules.name: The Flat Canvas Rule
rules.body: Only two surface colors exist in normal use: neutral-canvas behind everything, neutral-surface (white) for every actual content panel. Don't introduce a third background tone or a gradient panel; depth comes from the hover-glow and border system in Elevation, not from additional fills.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Every weight jump is Plus Jakarta Sans at a different size/weight, never a different family. A second typeface anywhere in this system is a regression, not an enhancement.

rules.name: The Hover-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: No element ships a resting shadow. If something needs to look elevated at rest, give it a tonal border or ring, not a shadow — shadows are reserved as a hover/interaction signal, and using one at rest would blunt that signal everywhere else.

dos: Do assign every PDF-related element Ink Indigo and every Image-related element Signal Emerald, token-for-token, per the One Lane Rule.
Do keep new panels flat with a tonal border at rest; add the lane-tinted glow shadow only as a hover/interactive response.
Do use Plus Jakarta Sans at every weight; rely on size/weight/color for hierarchy, not a second typeface.
Do keep the indigo-900 dark surface rare and bookend-only (hero, final CTA) so it stays a landmark, not wallpaper.
Do round every new UI element to one of the established steps (12px controls, 17px panels, full pills) — never an arbitrary radius.
donts: Don't add a resting box-shadow to a card, tile, or button; shadows exist only on hover in this system.

Don't blend indigo and emerald accents on the same component to signal "more important" — introduce a third named color instead if a genuinely new category is needed, and confirm it with the user first.

Don't introduce a third background fill between neutral-canvas and white neutral-surface, and don't use a gradient panel anywhere — the calm, flat-canvas feel is load-bearing for a tool that asks people to trust it with private files.
Don't add a watermark, paywall visual, or artificial-scarcity pattern to any tool output or CTA — this is a confirmed product/brand commitment, not just a visual preference.
